value: AUD patients showed increased connectivity between the right caudate and motor cortex compared with healthy controls.
Increased connectivity between the right caudate and motor cortex may reflect more likelihood of disinhibited and habitually-driven motor behaviors under stress.

name.value: Functional connectivity with the left LPFC seed

definition.value: AUD patients showed reduced connectivity with the dorsomedial PFC, but increased connectivity with sensory and motor cortices compared with healthy controls during stress; smoking status was additionally examined as a covariate.

spans.text: Neural correlates of positive and negative emotion regulation.

value: AUD participants showed significantly reduced connectivity with the dorsomedial PFC, but increased connectivity with sensory and motor cortices including the postcentral gyrus, precentral gyrus, and middle occipital gyrus.

Decreased connectivity between the left LPFC and DmPFC suggests reduced cognitive modulation of emotion and an inability to develop coping strategies in response to stress, while increased connectivity with sensory and motor cortices suggests greater susceptibility to emotional and motor-driven behaviors.

definition.value: Reduced connectivity between the left LPFC and dorsomedial PFC was associated with greater stress-induced anxiety in AUD patients.

value: Greater stress-induced anxiety was associated with reduced connectivity between the left DLPFC and DmPFC in AUD patients.
Reduced connectivity between the left LPFC and dorsomedial PFC could contribute to greater subjective anxiety response during stress.

spans.text: Using functional magnetic resonance imaging, brain responses of 37 AUD inpatients and 37 demographically-matched healthy controls were examined during brief individualized imagery trials of stress, alcohol-cue and neutral-relaxing conditions.

description.value: Participants underwent individualized stress, alcohol-cue and neutral-relaxing imagery trials during fMRI.

spans.text: For stress scripts

description.value: Individualized imagery of a highly stressful personal situation involving sadness, anger, upset, and inability to change the situation; scripts were based on scenarios rated at least 8 on a 10-point stressfulness scale and required emotional imagery.

spans.text: The alcohol cue script

description.value: Individualized imagery of a recent situation involving anticipation and consumption of alcohol, based on a reported occasion when the participant strongly wanted and then consumed an alcoholic drink; alcohol-cue situations involving negative affect or psychological distress were excluded.

spans.text: Neutral scripts were based on personal experience of neutral-relaxing situations

description.value: Individualized imagery of neutral-relaxing personal experiences, such as relaxing at the beach or reading on a Sunday afternoon; this was an active relaxing imagery comparison condition.

spans.text: An fMRI block design was used

instructions.value: Participants listened to and imagined individualized two-minute scripts for stress, alcohol-cue, or neutral-relaxing situations; during baseline and recovery they were instructed to remain still, and during recovery to stop imagining and lie still.

stimuli.value: Audio-taped, individualized imagery scripts presented through headphones: two stress scripts, two alcohol-cue scripts, and two neutral-relaxing scripts.
